name: Swiss Ball Push-Up Single-Leg
description: A swiss ball push-up performed with one foot lifted, reducing the base of support and dramatically increasing the demand on the core and hip stabilizers. The combination of the unstable ball surface and the single-leg stance requires sophisticated total-body coordination while still loading the pectoralis major and triceps through the pressing movement.

execution.starting_position: Begin in swiss ball push-up position (both hands on ball, both feet on floor, body in a plank). Lift one foot off the floor before beginning.
execution.setup_instructions: Fully inflate the ball. Place it on a non-slip surface. Master two-leg swiss ball push-ups before attempting this variation.
steps: Step 1: Establish the swiss ball plank with one foot lifted — the lifted leg is held straight and slightly elevated.
Step 2: Lower the chest toward the ball top, maintaining body control.
Step 3: Descend until the chest nearly touches the ball.
Step 4: Press back to the starting position. Maintain the single-leg balance throughout. Complete all reps then switch which leg is raised.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press.
common_mistakes: Hips rotating toward the lifted leg — keep them square
Attempting before mastering two-leg swiss ball push-ups
Placing the hands too far apart on the ball — keep them central on the ball top
safety_considerations: Fully inflate the ball — a soft ball deforms unpredictably under single-leg load
Have the ball against a wall as a stop if needed during learning
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range, same as two-leg version.
coaching_cues: The lifted leg is held still — do not let it swing or sway
Squeeze the ball inward with both hands to maximize shoulder stability
